note: Instrument identified from the paper, not from the table name: the dictionary Description calls this the 'D-block scale (unlabeled construct)', but the S1 .sav labels every d1-d9 column '主观幸福感' (subjective well-being) and the paper's sec. 2.2.2 names it as the Index of Well-Being (Campbell, Converse & Rodgers 1976) -- 9 items, 7-point, 8 general-affect semantic-differential pairs plus 1 life-satisfaction item, which is exactly the live shape (d1-d9, resp 1-7, 631 ids, 631 rows per item, no missing cells). Step 3b: no mismatch; the three sibling blocks in the same .sav are bullying (b1-12), academic adjustment (c1-30) and classroom environment (e1-25), and none of them is 9 items on 1-7. CODE DERIVATION: the IRW item code IS the .sav column name -- the build melts value_vars=['d1'..'d9'] with var_name='item' -- so there is no positional or renaming step. But the .sav's variable labels carry only the CONSTRUCT name, identical for all nine columns, and no value labels are attached to d1-d9, so the file does not tie any code to any wording; mapping_basis is therefore reconstructed, not data_labels. MAPPING: d1-d8 aligned to the instrument's published A-H order and d9 to the life-satisfaction item. Checked against the data by keying polarity (Step 5b route 6): the Chinese handbook rendering prints all eight affect pairs positive-adjective-first and then states '注：在实际问卷中将A，C，F，G项颠倒' (A, C, F, G are flipped in the actual questionnaire). That predicts exactly {d1,d3,d6,d7} keyed high=good and {d2,d4,d5,d8} keyed high=bad, and the live correlation matrix reproduces that partition exactly: r(d1,d3)=+.45, r(d1,d6)=+.41, r(d1,d7)=+.37, r(d1,d9)=+.11 vs r(d1,d2)=-.29, r(d1,d4)=-.11, r(d1,d5)=-.13, r(d1,d8)=-.18 (1 of 70 possible 4-of-8 partitions). The paper's own example anchor '1 = tiring, 7 = interesting' independently fixes the flipped direction of the 厌倦的/有趣的 pair. See verify_huang_2023_d_scale.R. It does NOT order items within either polarity class -- see the PARTIAL row in verification_huang_2023_d_scale.csv. TEXT: administered Chinese ships in the base fields (language=Chinese) with English in the _translated columns. The Chinese is a level-4 source -- a third-party reproduction of the standard Chinese 幸福感指数量表, not this study's own materials, which publish no item wording at all (the .sav has no item text at any label level and the article prints only the two examples quoted above). Two deliberate deviations, both disclosed: (a) the pole words are printed positive-left in the handbook and are shipped in the ADMINISTERED direction implied by the handbook's own flip note and confirmed by the data; (b) the handbook prints the life-satisfaction anchors as '十分满意 1 ... 7 十分满意' (a typo, the right pole should read 十分不满意) and says nothing about flipping it, but d9 keys with the positive class in the data (item-total +0.39 against the keyed total), so it is shipped as 1=十分不满意, 7=十分满意. SHAPE: item_text is BLANK for d1-d8 and all the words sit in option_text -- these are semantic-differential pairs with no question stem, the stemless shape the skill describes; audit_batch.R's 'blank item_text' WARN is expected here. Only resp 1 and 7 carry option_text; 2-6 were unlabeled in the instrument and are left blank rather than padded with their own number. instructions/section_prompt blank: neither the paper nor the handbook publishes participant instructions, and the two section headings are scoring labels (weights 1 and 1.1), not administered prompts. Two section_ids reflect the instrument's two real dimensions. translation_source=machine_translation: no published English of THIS Chinese rendering exists, so the _translated column is this project's literal English of the shipped Chinese; where the Chinese matches Campbell's original pair the English follows it (boring/interesting, useless/worthwhile, full/empty, hopeful, rewarding), and where the Chinese diverges the English follows the Chinese (d4 '朋友很多' = 'many friends', not Campbell's 'friendly'; d8 '生活对我太好了' = 'life has been very good to me', not 'brings out the best in me'). RIGHTS: PLOS deposit is CC BY 4.0; the Index of Well-Being is a 1976 academic instrument and no fee clause and no no-redistribution clause was found to quote, so neither 2026-09-04 trigger fires.
